summary: CD16 is used only as an NK subset marker; the paper concerns NK cell killing of CD4 T cells, not FCGR3B.
Mouse microglia CD16/32 marker in brain ageing and Alzheimer's disease; not about FCGR3B.
CD16 appears only as a macrophage phenotype marker in HIV-1 infection of vaginal mucosa; not about FCGR3B.

quote: MaterialWe have collated and selectively reviewed data on the most prominent well-established and emerging neutrophil-related biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets (calprotectin, lactoferrin, CXCR1, CXCR2, MMP-9, NGAL, elafin, HNE, pANCAs, MPO, CD16, CD177, CD64, HNPs, SLPI and PTX3) in ulcerative colitis.
summary: Review of neutrophil biomarkers and targets in ulcerative colitis that includes CD16 among many, without gene-specific data.
CD16 is only a monocyte subset marker in a miR-124 macrophage polarization study; not about FCGR3B.
Review of monocyte subsets defined by CD16 expression; not about FCGR3B.
Pexidartinib trial in solid tumors; CD16 only marks a monocyte subset, not about FCGR3B.
CD14+CD16+ monocyte expansion in hemodialysis patients; CD16 is a monocyte marker, not FCGR3B.
Crohn's disease macrophage subsets; CD16 only a monocyte phenotype marker, not about FCGR3B.

quote: Particularly important chemokines for activated/memory T cells are the CXCR3 ligands IP-10 and Mig and the CCR5 ligands RANTES, macrophage inflammatory protein-1alpha, and macrophage inflammatory protein-1beta.
summary: Paper concerns CXCR3 and CCR5 on T cells; Mig is named only as a CXCR3 ligand without specific results.

quote: CXCR3 is activated by three interferon-inducible ligands CXCL9 (MIG), CXCL10 (IP-10) and CXCL11 (I-TAC).
summary: Review of CXCR3 in T cell trafficking that names CXCL9 as one of three ligands.

quote: Among the differences in regulation, CXCL10 is induced by a variety of innate stimuli that induce IFN-α/β as well as the adaptive immune cell cytokine IFN-γ, whereas CXCL9 induction is restricted to IFN-γ.
summary: Review of CXCR3 ligands noting CXCL9 induction is restricted to IFN-gamma and its role in effector T cell trafficking.

quote: M1 macrophages release pro-inflammatory factors like tumor necrosis factoralfa (TNF-α), interleukin1alfa (IL-1α), interleukin1beta (IL-1β), interleukin6 (IL-6), C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 9 (CXCL9), and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10), while M2 macrophages secrete anti-inflammatory mediators including interleukin10 (IL-10), transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β), C-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CCL1), C-C motif chemokine ligand 17 (CCL17), C-C motif chemokine ligand 18 (CCL18), and C-C motif chemokine ligand 22 (CCL22).
summary: Review of MSC exosomes and M2 polarization; CXCL9 only appears in a list of M1 macrophage factors.

quote: CXCL9 promoted autoreactive T cell global recruitment to the skin but not effector function, whereas CXCL10 was required for effector function and localization within the skin.
summary: In a mouse vitiligo model CXCL9 promoted T cell recruitment to skin but not effector function; the paper focuses on CXCL10 and is not about colitis.

quote: An Ingenuity pathway analysis based on the differentially expressed genes suggested that propionate and butyrate modulate leukocyte trafficking, as SCFA strongly reduced the release of several pro-inflammatory chemokines including CCL3, CCL4, CCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11.
summary: Short-chain fatty acids reduced release of several chemokines from dendritic cells, with CXCL9 only one in the list.

quote: Only CXCL9 (MIG) inversely correlated with fatigue duration.
summary: In chronic fatigue syndrome serum, CXCL9 was the only cytokine inversely correlated with fatigue duration; not a UC study.

quote: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) analyses indicated abundant production of three chemokines, i.e. monokine induced by interferon-gamma (MIG), interferon-inducible protein 10 (IP-10) and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), in the DSS-irritated intestine of WT but not of IFN-gamma(-/-) mice.
summary: MIG (CXCL9) was abundant in inflamed DSS colitis intestine of wild-type mice but not IFN-gamma knockout mice, showing IFN-gamma-dependent production.

quote: Apremilast inhibited PBMC production of the chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10, cytokines interferon-gamma and tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, and interleukins (IL)-2, IL-12 and IL-23.
summary: Apremilast reduced PBMC output of CXCL9 among many cytokines in a psoriasis study; no gene-specific perturbation.

quote: The inflammatory chemokines CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11 are predominantly induced by interferon (IFN)-γ and share an exclusive chemokine receptor named CXC chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3).
summary: Review of the non-redundant activities of the interferon-inducible CXCR3 ligands including CXCL9.

quote: Both IP-10 and Mig, as well as the IFN-gamma-inducible T-cell alpha chemoattractant (I-TAC), which all share high-affinity binding for CXCR3, block HMVEC proliferation in vitro, an effect that can be inhibited by an anti-CXCR3 antibody.
summary: Mig, with IP-10 and I-TAC, blocked endothelial proliferation via CXCR3; focus is angiogenesis, not inflammation.

quote: We suggest that CXCL10 and possibly CXCL9 differ from other chemokines by their ability to restrain tumor growth and enhance anti-tumor immunity.
summary: Mini review of CXCR3 ligands in cancer and autoimmunity, suggesting CXCL9 may enhance anti-tumor immunity.

quote: Median increases in chemokine levels from baseline to C2D8 were 101% (CXCL9) and 37% (CXCL10) in peripheral blood.
summary: Nivolumab raised blood CXCL9 by a median of 101% in renal cancer patients, a pharmacodynamic change; not a UC study.

quote: This paper reviews all available information on hypoxia-induced changes in the expression of all CXC chemokines (CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCL3, CXCL4, CXCL5, CXCL6, CXCL7, CXCL8 (IL-8), CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CXCL12 (SDF-1), CXCL13, CXCL14, CXCL15, CXCL16, CXCL17) as well as CXC chemokine receptors-CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CXCR4, CXCR5, CXCR6, CXCR7 and CXCR8.
summary: Cancer hypoxia review covering all CXC chemokines; CXCL9 appears only in the list.

quote: We found that PRC2 components and demethylase JMJD3-mediated histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) repress the expression and subsequent production of Th1-type chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10, mediators of effector T-cell trafficking.
summary: In colon cancer cells PRC2 epigenetically represses CXCL9 and CXCL10 expression, limiting effector T-cell trafficking; cancer context, not UC.

quote: Microarray analysis of in vitro-derived macrophages treated with IFN-γ showed that many of the genes upregulated in macrophages were found in psoriasis, including STAT1, CXCL9, Mx1, and HLA-DR.
summary: CXCL9 is one of several IFN-gamma-induced macrophage genes also found in psoriasis; no gene-specific result.
